courses.title: Ethnographic Methods
courses.description: Exposes students to diverse methods, both traditional and experimental, used in anthropological ethnographic research. Students gain experience practicing diverse methods, and learn to select methods appropriate to particular study designs and contexts.

Students gain experience practicing diverse methods, and learn to select methods appropriate to particular study designs and contexts.

courses.description: Introduces research design for anthropology, including concept work and mapping, research topic and aims development, research question construction, and fieldwork planning.

courses.title: Ethnography
courses.description: Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 230F. Ethnography. 4 Units. Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies. Same as CRM/LAW C222 , CHC/LAT 217

courses.title: Transnational Migration
courses.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 235A. Transnational Migration. 4 Units. Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts. Same as SOC SCI 254A , CHC/LAT 215

courses.title: Black Ethnography in the Anthropological Imagination
courses.description: What is ethnography? Rather than an existential question, students cull through the history of the field and understand the very oft-problematic stance of ethnography to construction of particular types of blackness.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 236. Black Ethnography in the Anthropological Imagination. 4 Units. What is ethnography? Rather than an existential question, students cull through the history of the field and understand the very oft-problematic stance of ethnography to construction of particular types of blackness.

courses.title: Seminar in Political Anthropology
courses.description: Explores anthropological approaches to politics. Covers a range of issues and topics, including: theories of culture, power, and hegemony; approaches to colonial and post-colonial relations of global inequality; and ethnographic approaches to the modern state.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 245A. Seminar in Political Anthropology. 4 Units. Explores anthropological approaches to politics. Covers a range of issues and topics, including: theories of culture, power, and hegemony; approaches to colonial and post-colonial relations of global inequality; and ethnographic approaches to the modern state.

courses.title: Feminist Anthropology
courses.description: Examines feminist anthropology’s rise as an interdisciplinary field. Paying special attention to issues of power, subjectivity, and authority in the research encounter, feminist anthropologists’ major contributions to ethnography, gender studies, queer studies, and cultural anthropology are surveyed.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 246. Feminist Anthropology. 4 Units. Examines feminist anthropology’s rise as an interdisciplinary field. Paying special attention to issues of power, subjectivity, and authority in the research encounter, feminist anthropologists’ major contributions to ethnography, gender studies, queer studies, and cultural anthropology are surveyed.

courses.title: Structuralism and Post-Structuralism
courses.description: Traces recent theoretical discussions and arguments over the philosophical and historical "subject" from structuralist decenterings toward the characteristically "post-structuralist" contemporary concern with the historical and political constitution of subjectivities and subject positions.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 247A. Structuralism and Post-Structuralism. 4 Units. Traces recent theoretical discussions and arguments over the philosophical and historical "subject" from structuralist decenterings toward the characteristically "post-structuralist" contemporary concern with the historical and political constitution of subjectivities and subject positions.

courses.title: Archival Violence
courses.description: Synthesizes the multifaceted nature of the archive as both an object/tool of western ontological warcraft and as a driver/accelerator of difference making.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 248. Archival Violence. 4 Units. Synthesizes the multifaceted nature of the archive as both an object/tool of western ontological warcraft and as a driver/accelerator of difference making.

courses.title: Humanism and Posthumanism
courses.description: Examines alternative forms of human, humanisms, and posthumanisms to explore the inherent ambiguities and shifting boundaries of knowing and being human, and to venture into modes of analysis that problematize the universality and globality of liberal humanism.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 249A. Humanism and Posthumanism. 4 Units. Examines alternative forms of human, humanisms, and posthumanisms to explore the inherent ambiguities and shifting boundaries of knowing and being human, and to venture into modes of analysis that problematize the universality and globality of liberal humanism.

courses.title: Queer Anthropology
courses.description: Explores historical and contemporary scholarship that employs ethnographic approaches to address the discursive construction of sexuality. Also examines how the discipline of anthropology has been shaped by the study of sexuality.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 252A. Queer Anthropology. 4 Units. Explores historical and contemporary scholarship that employs ethnographic approaches to address the discursive construction of sexuality. Also examines how the discipline of anthropology has been shaped by the study of sexuality.

courses.title: Design, Aesthetics, and Social Life
courses.description: Anthropology has only recently recognized that design demands consideration as a cultural form linked to, yet nonetheless distinct from, other aesthetic endeavors. Largely oriented toward collaboratively working out a conceptual basis for a distinctly anthropological approach to design.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 253A. Design, Aesthetics, and Social Life. 4 Units. Anthropology has only recently recognized that design demands consideration as a cultural form linked to, yet nonetheless distinct from, other aesthetic endeavors. Largely oriented toward collaboratively working out a conceptual basis for a distinctly anthropological approach to design.

courses.title: Digital Anthropology
courses.description: Examines “the digital” from an anthropological perspective by exploring ethnographic research on digital culture and using anthropological frameworks to approach the digital and the human. Readings are interdisciplinary, including work from history and communications.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 254. Digital Anthropology. 4 Units. Examines “the digital” from an anthropological perspective by exploring ethnographic research on digital culture and using anthropological frameworks to approach the digital and the human. Readings are interdisciplinary, including work from history and communications.

courses.title: Disability Worlds
courses.description: Explores disability from a range of methodological and theoretical perspectives. Examines the genealogy of disability in anthropology and related disciplines, with an emphasis on ethnographic work. Topics addressed include access, embodiment, politics, selfhood, and sexuality.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 255A. Disability Worlds. 4 Units. Explores disability from a range of methodological and theoretical perspectives. Examines the genealogy of disability in anthropology and related disciplines, with an emphasis on ethnographic work. Topics addressed include access, embodiment, politics, selfhood, and sexuality.

courses.title: Ethnographies of Technology
courses.description: Surveys current ethnographic research pertaining to technologies, technical systems, and infrastructures.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 256A. Ethnographies of Technology. 4 Units. Surveys current ethnographic research pertaining to technologies, technical systems, and infrastructures.

courses.title: Secrecy, Security, and Surveillance
courses.description: Explores secrecy and security as fundamental to constructions of public and private domains, relations of citizenship and sovereignty, the militarization of everyday life, and the ways that the fabrics of societies are woven of both trust and deceit.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 256B. Secrecy, Security, and Surveillance. 4 Units. Explores secrecy and security as fundamental to constructions of public and private domains, relations of citizenship and sovereignty, the militarization of everyday life, and the ways that the fabrics of societies are woven of both trust and deceit.

courses.title: Dissertation Writing Seminar
courses.description: Intended for advanced, post-fieldwork Anthropology graduate students. Emphasis on the presentation of research design and results, problems of ethnographic writing, and qualitative and quantitative data and analysis. Prerequisites: post-fieldwork; graduate standing in Anthropology or consent of instructor.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 259A. Dissertation Writing Seminar. 4 Units. Intended for advanced, post-fieldwork Anthropology graduate students. courses.title: Critical Medical Anthropology
courses.description: Reading-intensive graduate seminar offers an overview of theoretical and ethnographic approaches to illness and healing in different settings, while also studying the political economic distribution of risks that contribute to disease. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 260. Critical Medical Anthropology. 4 Units. Reading-intensive graduate seminar offers an overview of theoretical and ethnographic approaches to illness and healing in different settings, while also studying the political economic distribution of risks that contribute to disease. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.

courses.title: Anthropology of the Mind
courses.description: Reading-intensive graduate seminar looks at emergence of mind/soul in modern age and similar concepts across cultural and historical contexts; studies psychiatric anthropological approaches to trauma, the subconscious, dreaming, madness. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 261. Anthropology of the Mind . 4 Units. Reading-intensive graduate seminar looks at emergence of mind/soul in modern age and similar concepts across cultural and historical contexts; studies psychiatric anthropological approaches to trauma, the subconscious, dreaming, madness. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.

courses.title: Black Political Theory in the United States
courses.description: Black Political Theory analyzes the development of Black political ideologies and the strategic processes by which Black people in the United States have attained freedom.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 263. Black Political Theory in the United States. 4 Units. Black Political Theory analyzes the development of Black political ideologies and the strategic processes by which Black people in the United States have attained freedom.

courses.title: Prisons in the United States
courses.description: Analyzes, deconstructs social relations and posits new realities with respect to interlocking violence that is levied against Black people in the form of prisons in the United States of America.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 263A. Prisons in the United States. 4 Units. Analyzes, deconstructs social relations and posits new realities with respect to interlocking violence that is levied against Black people in the form of prisons in the United States of America.

courses.title: Literary Anthropology
courses.description: Looks at genre-blending between creative nonfiction, ethnography, fiction, memoir and other forms of expression, interrogating the boundary between literature and ethnography.
courses.rawSourceText: ANTHRO 264. Literary Anthropology. 4 Units. Looks at genre-blending between creative nonfiction, ethnography, fiction, memoir and other forms of expression, interrogating the boundary between literature and ethnography.

courses.description: Introduces graduate students to the theoretical and practical aspects of teaching and learning in higher education. courses.description: Familiarizes students with the interrelated fields of criminology, law and society studies, and criminal justice studies. Organized around three well-established interdisciplinary literatures: criminology, sociolegal studies, and criminal justice studies.

courses.title: Legal Institutions and Society
courses.description: Acquaints students with the institutions of U.S. legal system and its operations, as well as with the constitutional framework undergirding this system, and defines the relationship between U.S. citizens and government at a variety of levels.

courses.title: Policing
courses.description: Introduces the subject of policing. Topics include the management of police organizations, the effectiveness of police patrol strategies, the experiences of women in policing, the recruitment and retention of police officers, and other related topics.

courses.description: Examines the major social scientific perspectives on criminal and deviant behavior. Specific deviant and criminal activities are described and explained using established theoretical frameworks.

courses.title: Public Policy, Crime, and Criminal Justice

Focuses on mechanisms of action, dose-response relationships, exposure pathways, and risk assessment. Includes applications in food safety, occupational health, environmental toxicology, regulatory policy, and health equity.

restrictions.raw: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

courses.rawSourceText: EHS 70. Toxicology and Society. 4 Units. Introduces principles of toxicology and societal implications of toxic exposures. Focuses on mechanisms of action, dose-response relationships, exposure pathways, and risk assessment. Includes applications in food safety, occupational health, environmental toxicology, regulatory policy, and health equity. Prerequisite: Recommended: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 5 Same as PUBHLTH 70 Restrictions: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

courses.title: Case Studies in Environmental Toxicology
courses.description: Explores toxicology principles through case-based discussions. Topics include exposure routes, absorption, metabolism, and mechanisms of toxicity. Lectures with discussions are delivered by invited faculty experts.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 201. Case Studies in Environmental Toxicology. 4 Units. Explores toxicology principles through case-based discussions. Topics include exposure routes, absorption, metabolism, and mechanisms of toxicity. Lectures with discussions are delivered by invited faculty experts. Prerequisite: EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-.
courses.prerequisiteRaw: EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-.

courses.title: Principles of Environmental Toxicology
courses.description: Explores molecular, biological, and structure-based toxicity of environmental toxicants. Topics include dose-response relationship, ADME, mechanisms of action, and its impact on the environment, wildlife, and human health. Covered through lectures, research papers, and discussion.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 202. Principles of Environmental Toxicology. 4 Units. Explores molecular, biological, and structure-based toxicity of environmental toxicants. Topics include dose-response relationship, ADME, mechanisms of action, and its impact on the environment, wildlife, and human health. Covered through lectures, research papers, and discussion.

courses.title: Occupational Epidemiology
courses.description: The importance of work environment for workers’ health and productivity has increased with changing technology, work organization, demographics, and occupation/industry structures. This advanced occupational epidemiology course focuses on work environment as exposures, and workers’ health and productivity as outcomes.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 203. Occupational Epidemiology. 4 Units. The importance of work environment for workers’ health and productivity has increased with changing technology, work organization, demographics, and occupation/industry structures. This advanced occupational epidemiology course focuses on work environment as exposures, and workers’ health and productivity as outcomes.

courses.title: Neurotoxicology
courses.description: The effects of various harmful chemicals upon nervous system function. Emphasis given to the molecular events underlying neurological damage and to the relation of such processes to basic mechanisms of neurobiology.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 204. Neurotoxicology. 4 Units. The effects of various harmful chemicals upon nervous system function. Emphasis given to the molecular events underlying neurological damage and to the relation of such processes to basic mechanisms of neurobiology.

courses.title: Target Organ Toxicology I
courses.description: Outlines vulnerability of selected organ systems to environmental and occupational chemicals. Reviews molecular aspects of toxicological damage. Topics include molecular toxicology and the following organ systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, dermal, and skeletal embryology.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 206A. Target Organ Toxicology I. 4 Units. Outlines vulnerability of selected organ systems to environmental and occupational chemicals. Reviews molecular aspects of toxicological damage. Topics include molecular toxicology and the following organ systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, dermal, and skeletal embryology. Same as PUBHLTH 277A

courses.title: Target Organ Toxicology II
courses.description: Analyzes mechanistic responses in animals and humans to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation, focusing on organ system physiology. Topics specifically covered include reproductive, endocrine, developmental, kidney, liver, pancreas, vascular, immune toxicology, radiation, and chemical carcinogenesis.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 206B. Target Organ Toxicology II . 4 Units. Analyzes mechanistic responses in animals and humans to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation, focusing on organ system physiology. Topics specifically covered include reproductive, endocrine, developmental, kidney, liver, pancreas, vascular, immune toxicology, radiation, and chemical carcinogenesis. Same as PUBHLTH 277B

courses.title: Experimental Design and Interpretation of Toxicology Studies
courses.description: Introduction to methods of structuring toxicology experiments and analyzing data, including experimental design, data distributions, sample sizes, hypothesis testing, linear regression, analysis of variance, multiple comparison testing, and non-parametric tests.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 207. Experimental Design and Interpretation of Toxicology Studies. 2 Units. Introduction to methods of structuring toxicology experiments and analyzing data, including experimental design, data distributions, sample sizes, hypothesis testing, linear regression, analysis of variance, multiple comparison testing, and non-parametric tests.

courses.title: Inhalation Toxicology
courses.description: Explores laboratory inhalation toxicology principles and practices. Covers aerosols, gases, respiratory tract structure/function, lung defenses, exposure techniques, experimental designs, animal models, and regulations/guidelines.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 212. Inhalation Toxicology. 4 Units. Explores laboratory inhalation toxicology principles and practices. Covers aerosols, gases, respiratory tract structure/function, lung defenses, exposure techniques, experimental designs, animal models, and regulations/guidelines.

courses.title: Industrial Toxicology
courses.description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 220. Industrial Toxicology. 4 Units. Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills. Prerequisite: PUBHLTH 277B with a minimum grade of B- or EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-. Same as PUBHLTH 278
courses.prerequisiteRaw: PUBHLTH 277B with a minimum grade of B- or EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
courses.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

restrictions.raw: School of Population and Public Health students only.

courses.rawSourceText: EHS 264. Introduction to Environmental Health Science. 4 Units. Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. courses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
courses.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 269. Air Pollution, Climate, and Health. 4 Units. courses.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
courses.description: Learn general principles and basic mathematical methods for environmental modeling and human health risk assessment, including compartmental and advection-dispersion models for contaminants in air and water, uptake by plants and animals, exposure, assessment, dose-response modeling, risk management, and risk perception.
courses.rawSourceText: EHS 275. Environmental Modeling and Risk Management. 4 Units. Learn general principles and basic mathematical methods for environmental modeling and human health risk assessment, including compartmental and advection-dispersion models for contaminants in air and water, uptake by plants and animals, exposure, assessment, dose-response modeling, risk management, and risk perception. Same as PUBHLTH 275

courses.title: Independent Study in Environmental Toxicology
courses.description: With consent from a faculty member who will supervise the program, a student may receive credit for individual study in some area of toxicology, culminating in the completion of a scholarly paper on the subject.

courses.description: Focus on theory and research in health psychology as applied to major acute, chronic, and occupational health problems.
